candidate_title: JANUS Resilient Edge Swarm: Low-Cost Heterogeneous Sensor and Telemetry Network for Degraded Connectivity

eligibility_reason.rfi_detailed_rule: small, for-profit, independent U.S. businesses with qualifying ownership/control and <=500 employees
eligibility_reason.webpage_conflict: summary field currently mentions small and large U.S.-based and allied foreign country businesses

primary_alignment: Command and Control (C2) and Counter-C2 Networks — resilient communications / deep sensing relevance
secondary_alignment: Adaptive Sustainment — distributed edge operations relevance
xtech_value_proposition: Freeze the physically existing heterogeneous swarm and convert current sensing, freshness, failure and recovery mechanisms into a reproducible evidence package that external evaluators can stress, measure, falsify and improve.
technical_differentiators: heterogeneous specialist roles rather than identical node images
protected local primary missions with bounded optional/shared work
observable loss, stale and recovery states
low-cost COTS hardware suitable for repeatable failure testing
inspectable source, provenance and claim boundaries
known_limitations: exact ten-device physical manifest not yet frozen
controlled xTech resilience and rejoin metrics not yet measured
2.4 GHz ESP-NOW/Wi-Fi-class transport is not a tactical anti-jam radio
military cybersecurity, fleet key management, accreditation and ATO not established
current COTS boards are not claimed ruggedized or MIL-STD-qualified
role-specific power and endurance not yet fully measured
scale beyond the actual tested physical fleet is unproven
heterogeneous firmware creates ABI, build and configuration complexity
some project lore, mining, game and multimedia functionality is outside the Army value proposition
commercial customers, revenue and quantified market traction are not documented
next_gates: obtain official Valid Eval DOCX template
physically identify all ten current nodes
freeze TEN_NODE_TEST_MANIFEST.json with exact board, firmware, commit and peripherals
collect dated group and per-node physical evidence
run quick reviewer demonstrator without modifying firmware during runs
run repeated full ten-node disruption and recovery evaluation
preserve successes, failures, raw logs and event timestamps
measure resource, thermal and power cost where instrumentation is available
promote only evidence-backed claims through CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX
transfer compressed final text into official three-page template
submit through Valid Eval only if eligibility is confirmed
